verdict.rationale: Better Auth is a code-first library with an official CLI (`npx auth init`, CLI-generated migrations) and server-side `auth.api` methods. Its auth config lives in version-controlled code with "no dashboard clicks", which suits scripted, headless use. However, nothing documents non-interactive CI runs. One hands-on report says admin scripts and tests were "very hacky" because of the request-header-based design, which limits the depth of support. Missing for 10: explicit CI or non-interactive CLI documentation (flags, exit codes, env-based config), documented headless or test-mode usage of server APIs without request headers, and independent corroboration of smooth CI automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: No dashboard clicks. Your auth lives in code version controlled, type-safe, and reviewable in PRs.
To authenticate a user on the server, you can use the `auth.api` methods.
